issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (UML and prose describe checkOrderReady with no parameters), but the solution implementation defines checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This parameter mismatch means students implementing the method as described in the exercise (no arguments) will produce a different signature than the solution/reference, leading to confusion and potential test/signature mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the reference implementation's method signature match the specification: change SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(boolean) to a no-argument method checkOrderReady(). Update internal calls (e.g., orderMeal should call checkOrderReady()) and remove the logging parameter or use an internal logging flag if needed. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to document the boolean parameter if it is intentional.

issues.description: The problem specification defines checkOrderReady() as a parameterless method (checkOrderReady(): void) that should be invoked after placing an order. In the solution implementation, checkOrderReady is given a different signature checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and is called with a boolean argument. This signature mismatch creates a conceptual mapping barrier: students will implement a parameterless method as required by the exercise, but the reference solution uses a different method signature (and the added parameter is unrelated to the core requirement). This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected method contract and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the problem signature by providing a parameterless checkOrderReady() method. Either remove the boolean parameter and any logging-specific argument from checkOrderReady, or add an overloaded parameterless checkOrderReady() that delegates to checkOrderReady(boolean) so the method contract in the problem statement (checkOrderReady()) and the implementation align.
